text.p: Here are highlights of stories in Romania's press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
Business:
CAPITAL
- The International Monetary Fund opposes Prime Minister Victor Ciorbea's plans to cut taxes, the newspaper says, commenting on the Fund's review mission to Romania.
- Romanian Development Bank (BRD) Vice President Petre Bunescu says in an interview that he foresees bank interest rates going down to 30 percent by year's end, based on current economic trends.
- A newspaper survey of the over-the-counter (OTC) market predicts slow interest in OTC trading until mid-August.
BURSA
- The newspaper prints a list of state companies, including oil refineries, which the Reform Ministry wants to close down, due to chronic losses.
- "The first negotiations with the IMF were the Golden Age of Prime Miinister Victor Ciorbea's government," says an editorial by political analyst Vladimir Pasti.

- The commodities exchange in the Transylvanian city of Sibiu plans to launch futures deals in hard currency on August 4, with the first futures deal quoting the leu-dollar rate over one- and three-month terms, the newspaper says.
ADEVARUL
- "We are resolved to push reform through the enterprises' gate," the newspaper quotes Reform Minister Ulm Spineanu as saying in an interview.
- State Ownership Fund president Sorin Dumitriu said he was not aware of a list of 12 companies up for liquidation issued by Reform Minister Ulm Spineanu.
General:
ROMANIA LIBERA
- Romanian President Emil Constantinescu appointed his adviser Catalin Harnagea to head the Foreign intelligence Service (SIE).

- Constantinescu sent birthday wishes to Romanian nationalist Ilie Ilascu -- detained by authorities in Moldova's breakaway Dnestr region. He saying he hoped Ilascu's 45th birthday would be his last in detention. The president's letter also says he pleaded Ilascu's case with the presidents of Ukraine and Moldova, Leonid Kuchma and Petru Lucinschi.
- High waters in the southern county of Gorj killed two women -- a mother and daughter -- on Tuesday night, the newspaper says.
ADEVARUL
- Dikes on the River Prut, on the border with ex-Soviet Moldova and the Somes, in the central Transylvanian region, and on the Danube could not withstand any new rise in levels,
- Reform Minister Ulm Spineanu told journalists he receives anonymous telephone calls and a woman is threatening his life.
-- Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
